tables.how: Every row of the lists of dealings with insiders (Schedule L) on WeHOPE's returns for tax years ending 2020 to 2024, latest version of each return. All 4 rows are on the return for 2024; the earlier returns list none. The building transaction of $4,555,548 is 33% of that year's total revenue of $13,701,397. 2 of the rows name an employee who is a relative of an officer and is not an officer; the name is on the return and is not printed here. A note on the same return (Schedule O, on Part VI line 2) says that the chief executive and the secretary, both founders, are married and that their two daughters are employed by the organization. The returns give the filer's name as “WE HOPE” and “WEHOPE”; they are one organization's by their employer identification number, 94-3342713.
tables.limits: The return does not say which officer or director the owner of Action Associates Inc is related to, what building was bought, from whom, or at what appraised value. It answers that the board approved the loan. It gives no such answer for the building transaction because the form has no approval question for business transactions: none of the 348 such rows on any return collected for this project carries one.  Nothing here shows that San Francisco money paid for it: the organization is also funded by other governments. A tax return is the organization's own statement, signed under penalty of perjury and not audited by the IRS. Its tax year is often not the City's fiscal year, and it counts money when earned or spent under its accounting method, not when the City paid. A disclosure on a return, including a dealing with an officer or a director, is what the law requires to be reported; the question is whether it is fair and approved.

Each organization's payments in the two tables the Controller publishes, as retrieved on 12 November 2026: Citywide Nonprofit Spending, which by its own description keeps contracted services only, and Vendor Payments (Vouchers), the table of every payment. The fiscal year is the one printed on the payment. Payee names are matched by the rule the organization pages use: the name without punctuation and company suffixes, plus the renames and spellings that a shared contract number confirms.
tables.limits: A payment is money the City sent, not money the organization kept or spent on itself: subsidies, rent aid and grants that an organization pays on to others are in these figures. The two tables differ where the nonprofit-spending table leaves out a kind of payment or a contract; neither is wrong for that reason. The year printed on a payment can be later than the year the payment was issued. A payee the City spells in a way that no contract number ties to the organization is not counted.
